subject: Vault Migration Spike — Kickoff
snippet: Following the architecture review decision to migrate to HashiCorp Vault, I've started the spike (DF...
body: Following the architecture review decision to migrate to HashiCorp Vault, I've started the spike (DF2LPE-538). Initial findings: we currently have 47 secrets spread across environment variables in Kubernetes and a legacy .env file system in the older services. The migration path is: stand up a Vault instance in our AWS account, migrate secrets service by service, update deployment configs, and remove the old env var approach. Vault Kubernetes auth is the right integration method here — services authenticate via their service account without needing a static Vault token. Estimated effort: 3 sprints for full migration. I'll have a detailed plan by end of week. One risk: the legacy Java services have secrets baked into JVM startup flags — those will need extra work. body: We've finalised the v2 mockups for the new analytics dashboard and would love your technical feedback before we move to the handoff phase. subject: PR Review Request: Rate Limiting Middleware
snippet: Could you review DF2LPE-502? It's the rate limiting middleware implementation. The PR adds a configu...
body: Could you review DF2LPE-502? It's the rate limiting middleware implementation. The PR adds a configurable sliding window rate limiter at the API gateway layer, using Redis for the counter storage. Key decisions I made that I'd like your input on: used a Lua script for the atomic counter increment and expiry — this avoids race conditions but ties us to Redis. Used a 429 response with Retry-After header (per RFC 6585). Configured default limits in environment variables rather than hardcoding. The PR has 18 commits (been iterating on the Redis key structure) but the final implementation is clean. Tests cover the happy path, rate exceeded path, and Redis unavailability fallback (passes through without limiting if Redis is down — intentional, fail-open for reliability). subject: Re: Slow Query Investigation — User Preferences Table
snippet: I've investigated the slow query on the user preferences table (DF2LPE-537). Root cause: the query t...
body: I've investigated the slow query on the user preferences table (DF2LPE-537). Root cause: the query that fetches all active A/B test assignments for a user does a full table scan because the composite index (user_id, experiment_id, status) is being ignored due to a function call on the status column in the WHERE clause (`LOWER(status) = 'active'`). Fix: either remove the LOWER() call (status values are already stored in lowercase) or add a functional index on LOWER(status). I recommend removing the LOWER() call — it's defensive code that doesn't add value. Query time drops from 340ms to 2ms with this change. I've opened a PR with the fix. Note: there are three other queries in the same file with the same pattern — I've fixed all of them in the same PR since the change is trivial. subject: HashiCorp Vault — Pricing and Licensing
snippet: Following the architecture decision to adopt HashiCorp Vault for secrets management, I've got the pr...
body: Following the architecture decision to adopt HashiCorp Vault for secrets management, I've got the pricing information you requested. Vault Community Edition is open source and free but lacks enterprise features (namespaces, HSM support, performance replication). Vault Enterprise starts at approximately $12,000/year for a small deployment. HCP Vault (managed cloud version) is $0.08 per secret per month plus compute, which would be approximately $3,000–5,000/year based on your estimated 47 secrets and usage patterns. Recommendation from procurement: start with Community Edition for the migration and evaluate whether you need enterprise features after 6 months of use. The main enterprise features you might need are namespaces (for multi-team isolation) and audit logging at scale. Let me know how you'd like to proceed and I'll get the contract started.
